incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Hosted API queue growth detected in us-west-2. GPU pool gpu-usw-1 at 98% alloc, p95 latency increased from 120ms -> 2.4s, p99 > 9s. Autoscaler attempted 3 provisioning cycles, failures reported: quota_limit_exceeded. Root ts=4449873210

Priya (oncall): taking this. paging Eli and Sam. Oncall details incoming.

Eli (infra): I see the provisioner logs. Errors around createInstance -> 403 QuotaExceeded from cloud provider. Provisioner retried and hit rate limits. GPU pool has no spare nodes to remove eviction backlog.

Sam (runtime-eng): runtime reports KV cache thrash and many long-running generative requests. Continuous batching is holding many requests open. If autoscaler can't get more GPUs we need to reduce concurrency and push fallbacks.

Maya (CS): flagging potential customer impact. A few support tickets from Acme and NovaApps reporting 503s and timeouts. They called into CS.

Priya (oncall): status: customers affected, partial. I'm opening bridge and will coordinate mitigations.

Priya (oncall): bridge -> https://meet.redwood/incident/4449873210 (joining) :phone:

Devon (prod-ops): quick mitigation options: 1) enable region fallback to eu-west for non low-latency traffic, 2) force-route traffic to quantized smaller model variant redwood-7b-q4 for best-effort customers, 3) global soft-429 for new sessions from unknown API keys. Which to apply first?

Sam (runtime-eng): prioritize model fallback for high-token requests. We can flip routing policy to prefer redwood-7b-q4 for request_size>1024 and for request_kind=completion. That will cut GPU token load by ~45%.

Eli (infra): quota appeal is in flight but will take time. Meanwhile I can reconfigure the provisioner to allow burst fallback to CPU-backed nodes for low-throughput workloads. Not great for latency but prevents timeouts.

Priya (oncall): steps: Sam implement routing change, Eli enable CPU fallback, Devon put soft-429 for new app_keys, Maya update CS. I'll annotate customer-impact and post update.

Sam (runtime-eng): doing routing flip now. Command pushed: 
```
rbctl route update --region us-west-2 --policy "prefer: redwood-7b-q4 if token_count>1024 or model_tag=best_effort"
```
Applying...

Sam (runtime-eng): routing change applied. Observability note: requests in backlog shifted to q4 models, queue length dropped ~30% in 90s.

Eli (infra): enabling CPU fallback for warm pools. Command: 
```
provisioner set-fallback --region us-west-2 --cpu-fallback true --max-warm-cpu 60
```
Output: accepted, but warm CPU pool spin-up will take ~60s.

Devon (prod-ops): enabling soft-429 for new keys. Config: 
```
throttle config update --global --new_keys_only --rate 5rps --response soft-429
```
Devon (prod-ops): applied. New key request rates limited, existing sessions unaffected.

Maya (CS): posting customer note to CS channel: Acme notified that we are experiencing degraded performance in us-west-2 and have shifted non-critical traffic to fallback models. Asking for priority customer list for manual whitelists.

Priya (oncall): current metrics after mitigations: queue length down 38%, p95 down to 480ms, p99 down to 1.6s, total error rate still elevated ~2.3% (was 8.7%). Good progress but not fully resolved.

Eli (infra): provisioner logs still show intermittent 403 on scale-up. Cloud quota reached for the account; appeal ticket 987654 opened with priority. Estimated resolution 2-6 hours. Need durable mitigations if appeal delayed.

Sam (runtime-eng): additional steps: enable prefix KV cache TTL extension to reduce recompute for active sessions, and aggressively compress KV keys for low-memory models. Pushing small runtime patch now.

Priya (oncall): apply runtime patch. Sam please post diffs and commands.

Sam (runtime-eng): patch applied: 
```
runtime-config set --kv-ttl 90s --kv-compress true --apply prod:us-west-2
```
Patch shows immediate reduction in token amplification for streaming responses.

Maya (CS): CS update posted: customers with degraded traffic may see lower-quality or slower responses; major customers Acme and NovaApps have been whitelisted to remain on full models. Other customers automatically routed to q4 best-effort.

Priya (oncall): customer impact estimate: ~7% of requests saw 5xx/timeouts at peak; ~1.1% still failing post mitigation; impacted customers list collected. We'll follow up with support postmortem.

Devon (prod-ops): recommending follow-up: enact autoscaler backoff protections to avoid hot re-provisioning loops, and add a temporary override to allow burst-scaling beyond soft quota for 20 mins if appeal remains pending. Need exec sign-off for quota override.

Eli (infra): taking logs snapshot and uploading to incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/4449873210/logs.tar.gz

Priya (oncall): handover plan: I'm staying with bridge for 30 more minutes, then Eli will be primary for infra until quota ticket resolves, Sam will handle runtime regressions, Devon will watch global rate rules, Maya will coordinate customer comms.

Priya (oncall): Post-incident actions noted: 1) add autoscaler graceful degrade policy 2) monthly quota safety buffer 3) improve routing rules for high token requests 4) update CS runbook.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: severity=high, impact=partial, incident-id=INC-2026-4449873210

Priya (oncall): closing bridge for now as mitigations are holding. We'll reopen if error rate climbs. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:

Maya (CS): I'll follow up with detailed customer impact doc and send to stakeholders.

Eli (infra): leaving a watch on quota ticket. If we get green light for temporary quota bump I'll notify and scale.

Sam (runtime-eng): logging follow-up items to runtime backlog: KV tuning, fallback perf tests, add canary for routing flips.

Devon (prod-ops): adding temporary dashboard for autoscale-fail events and throttle counts.

Priya (oncall): last check 4449873350: error rate stabilized at 1.1%, p95 420ms, p99 1.5s. I'll create formal incident report later.

incident-bot: Note: next steps assigned to Priya, Eli, Sam, Maya, Devon.
